<div class="no-left-nav"></div>

Welcome! Building a civic tech project is more than building a tool. It means understanding a real problem, working with communities, bringing people together, and creating something that can last.

We’re excited you’re interested in starting a Civic Tech Project. Not every project needs to be fully formed before you come to us. Depending on where your project is right now, you may start in either the **Onboarding Track** or the **Incubator Track**. But first:

## Is Your Project a Good Fit?

Before getting started, make sure your project fits the type of work Civic Tech DC supports.

### Who We Work With

We welcome projects from:

- **Nonprofits or Organizations:** Our strongest partners historically have been local nonprofits and community-based organizations. Whether it’s digitizing paper processes, building new forms, or building proofs-of-concept, we’re always interested in seeing how we can use technology to make an impact in our community.
- **Government:** Local government provides invaluable services and help to our community and we’re interested in helping make it more effective. This might mean developing a community outreach and feedback project, building a tool for people to request a particular service, or building some other proof-of-concept for how government interacts with its constituents.
- **Community Members:** Do you have an idea of how technology could help solve a problem in your community? We’re interested in hearing more! Those close to or experiencing a problem in our community likely know it best and have ideas for how it can be improved.

### What We Don’t Take On

- **Electoral or partisan campaign work:** Civic Tech DC does **not** support campaigns, candidates, or electoral advocacy. We are strictly nonpartisan. Projects may address public issues or policy topics, but they must remain focused on public-interest outcomes rather than campaigning.
- **Startup product development for private benefit:** We do not accept pitches that ask volunteers to build or advance privately owned startup products. Volunteer time is reserved for public-interest projects.
- **Ideas clearly not intended for public interest or without a clear community need:** Projects should have a clear benefit to a community, nonprofit, public agency, or other public-interest purpose.
- **Projects requiring resources Civic Tech DC cannot realistically provide:** Some projects require specialized staff, significant funding, proprietary technology, or other resources that are outside the capacity of a volunteer-driven project.
- **Unrealistic deadlines:** We cannot guarantee that a volunteer team will meet an externally imposed deadline. If a project depends on a fixed deadline, the scope and timeline need to be realistic for a volunteer team. If the deadline is critical, it may be better to work with another organization or professional service provider.

**Not sure if your project fits?** That’s okay. These criteria are meant to help us understand whether Civic Tech DC is the right home for your project, not to discourage ideas. If you are unsure, bring your idea to a Project Night or reach out to the organizers. We can help you think through the problem.

## Participation Pathways

Projects come to Civic Tech DC from two directions: **community-initiated** or **volunteer-initiated**. 

This categorization helps determine what support the potential projects needs. For example, community-initiated projects often have a defined problem and an existing partner, while volunteer-initiated projects may need more time to develop the ideaor define the project’s first milestone. Regardless of where a project starts, we work with the project to set a realistic scope and expectations for volunteers.

### Community-Initiated

You are a nonprofit, government agency, community organization, or other partner that has identified a problem and is looking for volunteers to help address it. This might look like:

- **Open need:** We have a problem or need and are looking for volunteers to help explore or build a solution.
- **Specific request:** We have a defined request with a deadline, requirements, or acceptance criteria.

### Volunteer-Initiated

A individual, who is willing to be the lead for a project, has identified a problem or opportunity and wants to develop a project around it. This might look like:

- **Idea without a partner:** I have an idea but have not yet identified an organization or community partner.
- **Partnered idea:** I have an idea and already have a community or organizational partner.

## Project Criteria

Projects that become Civic Tech DC projects should meet the following criteria. These criteria help us determine whether a project is a good fit and where it should start.

<table>
  <thead>
    <tr>
      <th></th>
      <th>Criteria</th>
      <th>Details</th>
    </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
    <tr>
      <td>✔</td>
      <td><strong>It’s civic tech</strong></td>
      <td>
        The project relates to civic life in a meaningful way. See our
        <a href="/learn/"> definition of civic tech</a>.
      </td>
    </tr>

    <tr>
      <td>✔</td>
      <td><strong>It’s open source</strong></td>
      <td>
        Projects must be open source so volunteers can contribute. Code and other project materials should be accessible to the community.
      </td>
    </tr>

    <tr>
      <td>✔</td>
      <td><strong>It serves a real community or partner</strong></td>
      <td>
        There is a clear end user such as a community, nonprofit, public agency, or other public-interest partner whose needs the project is addressing.
      </td>
    </tr>

    <tr>
      <td>✔</td>
      <td><strong>It has a public-interest purpose</strong></td>
      <td>
        The project is intended to create a benefit beyond the individual contributors or organization building it.
      </td>
    </tr>

    <tr>
      <td>→</td>
      <td><strong>Onboarding Track</strong></td>
      <td>
        You have a clear problem, a community or organizational partner, a project lead, and a defined goal or first milestone.
      </td>
    </tr>

    <tr>
      <td>→</td>
      <td><strong>Incubator Track</strong></td>
      <td>
        You need to find a partner, identify a project lead, or clarify the problem or first milestone before the project is ready for a volunteer team.
      </td>
    </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>

Once you've determined that your project is a good fit, the next step is to choose the track that matches where you are.

<h2>Choose Your Track </h2>

- **Ready to go?** Start with the **Onboarding Track**.

- **Still figuring things out?** Start with the **Incubator Track**.

If you're not sure, come to a Project Night and talk with the Civic Tech DC organizers. <strong>We may also recommend a different track depending on the project’s needs and readiness.</strong>
